name: Bamenyam
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Forku, Doris Tsafack (2000) grammar sketch of Bamenyam (Univ. Yaounde memoire, 116pp); Ndedje 2003 La morphologie nominale du Mengambo; neither online.

new_statements.quote: [p.9] The Màmə́nyán language is a tone language. Without this tone, it will be impossible to get the meaning of a word since we found many words in the language which differ only in their tones. [p.15] As a tone language, Màmə́nyán has the pitch phenomenon of tone which functions in the language as a feature associated with vowels and syllabic nasals. [p.95] After the examination of tones, four tonemes were attested: the H tone, the L tone, the HL tone and the LH tone.
new_statements.citation: Tsafack Forku, Doris. 2000. A Sketch of the Phonology of Mamenyan and Standardization Perspectives. MA thesis, Université de Yaoundé I.
new_statements.locator: sec. 0.7 'Typology', p.9 (PDF p.20); ch.1 'Tones', p.15 (PDF p.26); General Conclusion, p.95 (PDF p.106)

(2) p.15 (PDF p.26), ch.1 Tones: "As a tone language, Màmə́nyán has the pitch phenomenon of tone which functions in the language as a feature associated with vowels and syllabic nasals." -- verbatim; then 1.1 Inventory of tones: level (high, low) a…
new_statements.rule_in_words: The language is described purely as a tone language with four lexical tonemes (H, L, HL falling, LH rising) carried by vowels and syllabic nasals; the description makes no statement of any kind about word stress or accent (neither a position nor a denial). Ndedje 2003 (p.26) independently says the same: 'mə̀ŋgambo est une langue à tons', four tonemes H, B, BH, HB, again with no stress statement.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the conclusion (p.95-96) lists upstep, downstep and downdrift as tonal phenomena left for future study.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation-form words (1,300-item corpus); no word- or phrase-level stress/accent domain is discussed in either thesis.
new_statements.identity_note: Both theses describe the speech of Bamenyam village (25 km from Mbouda, Bamboutos Division, West Region, Cameroon), ALCAM code 908, Ethnologue/ISO bce = Glottolog bame1260. Forku 2000 calls it Màmə́nyán (autonym); Ndedje 2003 calls it mə̀ŋgambo/Mengambo (another name for the same village language, per his sec. on ALCAM 908 and Ethnologue BCE). No dialect split is described.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 0.7 Typology (p.9) and Ch.1 Tones (pp.15-19): Màmə́nyán is a tone language with four tonemes (H, L, HL, LH) borne by vowels and syllabic nasals; syllable chapter (p.60-61) defines the nucleus by tone; conclusion (p.95) restates four tonemes and names upstep/downstep/downdrift for future work. The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur in a prosodic sense anywhere in the text layer.

sources.note: Nothing. Ch.1 phonological overview, sec. 1.3 Les tons (p.26): 'mə̀ŋgambo est une langue à tons', two level (H/B) and two contour (BH/HB) tones, all four are tonemes; sec. 2.4.1.2 gives tonal schemes of noun roots. No mention of accent/stress (only the idiom 'mettre l'accent sur').
